text:
Mira: Quick design review — bulk revoke flow in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz. Thinking progressive disclosure for long lists to avoid accidental mass revokes. Thoughts?
Alex: +1. Show selected count in header and collapse details: show first 2 items then 'Show all (N)'. That reduces cognitive load.
Sam: Accessibility: ensure keyboard multi-select (shift + arrow/space) and SR reads 'X of Y selected' when toggling select-all. Use aria-live.
Jordan: Also mobile: safety banner needs to be sticky above the action buttons. Inline banners get lost.
Kevin: For scale: >10 keys -> prominent warning, >50 keys -> require typing 'REVOKE' to confirm. Could be a setting for orgs.
Alex: Agree on tiered confirmation. Also consider a 'dry run' summary screen listing keys that will be revoked to avoid surprises.
Sam: Toast after revoke should be `Revoked 12 keys. Undo` with aria-live assertive and keyboard focus goes back to table. 10s undo.
Mira: Question: primary button order — should destructive be primary on right or left? Our pattern currently primary on right (confirm) but product has mixed signals.
Jordan: Keep consistent with patterns: primary on right, but make destructive style distinct (red) and add accessible label `Confirm revoke of X keys`.
design-bot: Accessibility checklist: focus order, aria-labels on 'select all', `aria-live="polite"` for selection count, `aria-live="assertive"` for final toasts. Add keyboard shortcuts doc.
Mira: I'll update the file with: tiered confirmations, collapsed list + show all, SR copy and toast behaviors. Ping me if you want to test with NVDA/VoiceOver. :thumbsup: 
Alex: Thanks — leaving a quick note to QA to test selection SR messages and undo timing.
Sam: I'll file a small test plan. — Sam
